summary: Both tickets' own code and unit/component-level tests hold up under re-run: #981's generic structured-detail carrier (workRoutes.ts's refusalDetail()/workErrorResponse(), lib/work/api.ts's carrier(), trade-invoice-form.tsx) and #980's shared-harness ask_question script (work-journal-serve.mjs) are exactly as the report describes, and every unit-level claim reproduces exact test counts: work-routes-unit.test.mjs 28/28, lib/work/api.test.ts 26/26, work-journal-db.test.mjs (PGPORT 55750/clara_l10) 23/23, the four-file runtime unit combination 79/79, the whole apps/web unit suite 4637 tests/135 suites/4635 pass/0 fail/2 skip, pnpm typecheck exit 0, pnpm lint exit 0, check-frozen-workflows.mjs (no manifest diff, none of the lane's files in --print-closure) and check-parts-parity.mjs both OK. TDD discipline is real: ba4071de/eb542765/14b67ddf show a genuine red-then-green-then-wire-fix sequence, and LEGACY_BODIES plus the 981.web negative-detail cells are non-vacuous (they pin the pre-#981 shape byte-for-byte as well as the new carrier). No migration, no PRD/ARCHITECTURE edit, no frozen module, commits name their tickets, scope holds. HOWEVER: re-running the two heavy World e2e files that carry #980's own acceptance criteria produced inconsistent results across repeated attempts on this shared Windows rig. A clean, isolated run of trade-invoice-e2e.mjs (attempt 4 of 4) passed all 7 legs exactly as the report claims, including both new legs (6: park+replay+answer convergence; 7: commit-window cancel with zero journal effect) — the three earlier attempts each failed with a DIFFERENT symptom while running concurrently with another heavy process, which points to rig contention rather than a lane defect. More concerning: an isolated, solo re-run of work-journal-e2e.mjs (nothing else running) FAILED at its leg 4 (the narrate leg, AC4 of #980's own acceptance criteria: 'every existing post/narrate World test still passes unchanged') with 'a run that produced nothing is FAILED, not completed (got completed)'. Reading work-journal-serve.mjs shows the narrate branch returns immediately, before the new ask_question branch's code, so lane10's diff cannot structurally reach or alter that path — but this reviewer's shared database (clara_l10) had accumulated ~80+ Work rows from repeated e2e attempts made during this review, which RIG.md itself flags as a source of downstream interference (rig-isolation.test.mjs T10b, World-bootstrap side effects). The report's own single clean run claimed 'all 8 legs green in 41s'; this reviewer's re-run contradicts that on the exact leg AC4 depends on, and the cause could not be conclusively isolated to either a pre-existing environmental flake or lane pollution from this review's own repeated testing. Recommend one fresh-database confirmatory run before treating AC4 as fully closed; no code change to the lane's own diff appears warranted since the affected code path is unreachable from this lane's changes.

findings.title: AC4 ('every existing post/narrate World test still passes unchanged') did not reproduce on an isolated re-run of work-journal-e2e.mjs
findings.evidence: Solo run (PGHOST=127.0.0.1 PGPORT=55750 PGDATABASE=clara_l10, nothing else running concurrently): `node tests/work-journal-e2e.mjs` printed PASS 1/2/3/6/7/8 then failed with `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: a run that produced nothing is FAILED, not completed (got completed)` at work-journal-e2e.mjs:696 (the narrate leg, leg 4). The report claims 'all 8 legs green in 41s' from its own single run. Reading packages/runtime/tests/work-journal-serve.mjs's doGenerate: `if (SCRIPT === "narrate") { return {content:[{type:"text",...}], finishReason:{unified:"stop"}, ...}; }` returns unconditionally before the file reaches the new `if (SCRIPT === "ask_question")` branch added by this lane, so the narrate code path is structurally unreachable from this lane's diff — the failure is very unlikely to be a regression this lane introduced, but it does mean the specific claim 'measured' for AC4 is not reliably reproducible, and this reviewer's clara_l10 database held ~80 accumulated Work rows from five earlier e2e attempts made during this same review session, which is a plausible confound RIG.md itself names (rig-isolation.test.mjs T10b, World-bootstrap side effects) but which this reviewer could not rule out without a from-scratch database.
findings.required_fix: Before closing #980, run tests/work-journal-e2e.mjs once more, alone, on a freshly migrated/seeded database (not one reused across many e2e attempts), and record the result. If it still reds on the narrate leg, file the flake as its own ticket (it predates and is independent of this lane's diff) rather than reopening #980; if it passes clean, note the confirmatory run in the lane's final report. No change to this lane's own commits is indicated.

findings.title: trade-invoice-e2e.mjs (carries #980's own new legs 6 and 7) is sensitive to concurrent World-e2e/process contention on this shared rig
findings.evidence: Three re-run attempts of tests/trade-invoice-e2e.mjs, each overlapping with another heavy process this reviewer had started (pnpm typecheck; a concurrent work-journal-e2e.mjs run; residual state from the prior two attempts), failed with three DIFFERENT symptoms: attempt 1 failed leg 7's `stopping` status assertion (`GET` already read `cancelled`); attempt 2 failed leg 6 with `the run never asked a question` (a 90s poll timeout); attempt 3 failed leg 4 (pre-existing, unrelated to #980/#981) with `timeout waiting for serve child exit`. A fourth, isolated run (nothing else running concurrently besides the unrelated apps/web unit suite) passed all 7 legs cleanly — `6 OK — parked on a question, replayed into the window, answered, ONE of everything`, `7 OK — cancelled inside the commit window; no journal effect`, `PASS — all legs green`, exit 0 — matching the report exactly, including both of #980's new legs.
findings.required_fix: No fix to this lane's code. Worth a note to the orchestrator/integration step: do not run this lane's (or another lane's) heavy World e2e concurrently with another World e2e or a full typecheck/lint pass on the same physical rig; RIG.md already documents an analogous Windows contention precedent for `next build` (#869, retry once) and this reviewer's experience suggests the same applies to the World e2e child-process/DB layer.
